title: Repeated Windows Application Error Crashes
exclusions: Detects at least four `Application Error` Event ID 1000 records for the same host, faulting application, module, and exception code in one closed 30-minute window. Four is a local starting threshold. It excludes Event 1002 hangs, Event 1001 WER buckets/system bugchecks, single crashes, crashes whose application cannot be extracted, custom crash reporters, dump analysis, root-cause attribution, and user-impact proof. A faulting module can be a victim rather than cause. No dump collection, restart, runtime validation, or SME assurance is claimed.
evidence: Retain `windows_repeated_application_error_1000`, schedule/dispatch/alert history, result count/host/app/module/exception/time/record IDs, raw Application XML/messages, application/version/deployment ownership, source health, input/add-on versions, positive/boundary controls, alert delivery, incident disposition, and any approved dump metadata or bounded exception. This review caused no crash, dump, search job, or alert.

controlTest.positiveScenario: Insert four XML Application events inside the closed 30 minutes with provider `Application Error`, EventCode 1000, host `APP01`, distinct EventRecordIDs, and messages containing faulting application `orders.exe`, module `orders.dll`, exception `0xc0000005`. Expect one row with `crash_count=4` and those normalized dimensions.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Expect zero rows separately for exactly three matching crashes; four Event 1002 hangs; four ID 1000 events from another provider; four crashes split across modules or exception codes with no group reaching four; missing application extraction; and events in the newest excluded five minutes.

dataSources: Windows Application XML, provider `Application Error`, Event ID 1000, collected via Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Windows (Splunkbase 742) as `sourcetype=XmlWinEventLog`, `source=XmlWinEventLog:Application`, deployment-local `index=wineventlog`. Required fields: `_time`, `Computer`/`host`, provider, `EventCode`/`EventID`, `EventRecordID`, `Level`, `Message`; application/module/exception/version/path extraction must be validated against each supported event template/locale.
app: Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Windows (`Splunk_TA_windows`, Splunkbase 742), reviewed at 10.0.1.
spl:
index=wineventlog sourcetype="XmlWinEventLog" source="XmlWinEventLog:Application" EventCode=1000 earliest=-35m@m latest=-5m@m
| eval event_id=tonumber(coalesce(EventCode,EventID)), provider=lower(trim(coalesce(Provider_Name,SourceName))), host=lower(trim(coalesce(Computer,dest,host))), message=coalesce(Message,RenderedDescription,_raw)
| where event_id=1000 AND provider="application error" AND len(host)>0
| rex field=message max_match=1 "(?im)^Faulting application name:\s*(?<faulting_application>[^,\r\n]+)"
| rex field=message max_match=1 "(?im)^Faulting module name:\s*(?<faulting_module>[^,\r\n]+)"
| rex field=message max_match=1 "(?im)^Exception code:\s*(?<exception_code>0x[0-9a-f]+)"
| eval faulting_application=lower(trim(faulting_application)), faulting_module=lower(trim(coalesce(faulting_module,"not_extracted"))), exception_code=lower(trim(coalesce(exception_code,"not_extracted")))
| where len(faulting_application)>0
| stats count as crash_count min(_time) as first_seen max(_time) as last_seen values(EventRecordID) as event_record_ids values(Level) as levels values(source) as observed_sources by host faulting_application faulting_module exception_code
| where crash_count>=4
| eval threshold_crashes=4, window_minutes=30, threshold_basis="local starting policy"
| convert ctime(first_seen) ctime(last_seen)
| table host faulting_application faulting_module exception_code crash_count threshold_crashes window_minutes first_seen last_seen event_record_ids levels observed_sources threshold_basis
| sort 0 -crash_count host faulting_application
description: Reports a host/application/module/exception combination when at least four Application Error 1000 crashes occur in the closed 30-minute interval from 35 to 5 minutes before dispatch. Each row preserves count, first/last time, record IDs, levels and source identity for repeat-failure triage.
value: Repeated crashes of one executable signature can reveal a bad release, dependency, driver interaction, corrupted state, or workload-specific defect before scattered user tickets are connected. A stable signature and raw records help application owners compare deployment timing and decide whether controlled dump collection is warranted. This shortens service-restoration work by grouping recurring failures around the executable signature responders must diagnose.
implementation: Collect Application XML, validate Event 1000 provider/message extraction, save `windows_repeated_application_error_1000`, and run every 30 minutes over a five-minute delayed closed window. Trigger at four or more matching signatures, tune per application after replay, correlate deployment/user impact, and collect dumps only through an approved application-specific WER or debugger runbook.
visualization: Show Application-source freshness, top crashing applications/signatures, trend by host, and result table. Drilldown to raw 1000 plus related WER 1001 and deployment/service events; keep dump paths and sensitive artifacts access-controlled.
schema: Native Windows Application Error Event 1000 XML/message
dataModelAcceleration: No Application_State tstats equivalent is claimed because it may not retain provider, module, exception and EventRecordID. Summaries require signature parity and source completeness.

knownFalsePositives:
Rows are real repeated crashes; impact/authorization determines action.

1. **Azure DevOps/Jenkins/Octopus deployment test** — Match release/run, canary host, expected crash injection and UTC window. Preserve result; suppress only exact app/host/release timebox.

2. **Microsoft Application Verifier or WinDbg test** — Diagnostic instrumentation can intentionally terminate a process. Confirm debugger/operator/case and test asset.

3. **IIS application-pool recycle with failing health probe** — Repeated worker startup failures can look like a crash storm. Correlate pool/process start, HTTP health and deployment; fix startup and use bounded exception only during approved test.

4. **Vendor updater rollback loop** — Microsoft/Adobe/Java or line-of-business updater can repeatedly launch a bad binary. Verify package/version/installer logs and stop the approved deployment loop rather than allowlisting.

5. **Security product exploit-prevention test** — Defender/EDR may terminate a test process. Match product event, policy/test ID and responder.

**Safe suppression:** post-result `lookup windows_app_crash_notification_exceptions.csv` keyed by exact `host,faulting_application,faulting_module,exception_code,exception_id` with numeric validity bounds and owner/approver.
mitreAttack: N/A (application reliability monitoring; no ATT&CK behavior asserted)
reviewer: documentation-only Cursor AI editorial review against Microsoft application crash and WER dump documentation plus Splunk Windows add-on documentation; crashes, field extraction, SPL, controls, thresholds, alerts, dumps, debugging, and remediation not executed or SME-signed

cost.search_load_notes: One provider/Event ID over 30 closed minutes; event volume is normally low.

detailedImplementation:
## Prerequisites and scope

Assign application, Windows, Splunk, release, incident and dump/evidence owners. Inventory critical executables, hosts, versions and service owners. Install `Splunk_TA_windows` (Splunkbase 742); grant a read-only role to `index=wineventlog`. Dumps can contain secrets and require separate restricted storage/RBAC.

Microsoft identifies Application Error 1000 as the actual crash event and WER 1001 as related reporting/bucket information. Event 1002 is a hang and needs another rule. The faulting module and exception are a signature, not root cause; Microsoft troubleshooting proceeds to updates, event review and controlled dump analysis.

## Collection and extraction

Configure `[WinEventLog://Application]`, `renderXml=true`, deployment-local `index=wineventlog`, and checkpoint interval 5 in a managed `local/inputs.conf`. Validate `source=XmlWinEventLog:Application`, `sourcetype=XmlWinEventLog`; prevent direct/WEF duplicates and preserve Computer. Compare fixed EventRecordIDs with Event Viewer:

```spl
index=wineventlog sourcetype="XmlWinEventLog" source="XmlWinEventLog:Application" EventCode=1000 earliest=-7d
| table _time Computer Provider_Name EventRecordID Level Message
```

Test message extraction for every supported OS locale/template. If XML exposes named fields, prefer verified aliases; do not use generic `Application` or `param1` without proving meaning. Missing application is excluded and must create a data-quality finding.

## Search and controls

Save `windows_repeated_application_error_1000`; schedule every 30 minutes with `earliest=-35m@m latest=-5m@m`. Measure latency and retain nonoverlapping windows. Group by host/application/module/exception. Four is minimum because predicate is `>=4`; it is a local policy, not Microsoft guidance. Do not combine hosts or app versions blindly.

Replay positive and all negatives, including provider collision, exact threshold, split signatures, missing extraction and latest boundary. In a lab use a purpose-built crash executable and approved account; do not crash production. Record OS/app/add-on/Splunk versions, XML, fixture hash, bounds, expected/actual rows, job ID and alert delivery. Keep draft until human acceptance.

## Triage and dump handling

Verify source freshness/raw EventRecordIDs; identify executable/version/deployment and user/service impact; inspect adjacent WER 1001, service, update, resource and EDR events; compare signature across fleet; reproduce safely. Microsoft documents application-specific `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\Windows Error Reporting\LocalDumps\app.exe` with DumpFolder, DumpCount and DumpType. Enable only through change control, set folder ACL/retention/capacity, reproduce, disable or retain by policy, hash and restrict dumps, then analyze with approved symbols/tools.

Do not automatically restart services, recycle IIS, uninstall updates, disable antivirus, run SFC/DISM, or enable full dumps fleet-wide. Full dumps can be large and expose credentials/data. A common DLL can be the crash victim.

## Troubleshooting

- No events: verify Application input/provider/index/RBAC, source health and whether the application uses custom reporting.
- Extraction null/localized: inspect raw message/XML and build tested locale extraction; do not merge unknown applications.
- Duplicate counts: identify direct/WEF duplicates via Computer/EventRecordID/time.
- Expected row absent: check closed bounds, provider exactness, signature split and four-event threshold.
- Many signatures after release: enrich app version/deployment and compare canary/control hosts.
- No dump: verify application supports WER LocalDumps, service/configuration, folder ACL, DumpCount/Type and available storage.
- Dump exists: protect as sensitive evidence; event data alone does not replace debugger analysis.
grandmaExplanation: We notice when the same program crashes with the same basic signature four or more times in half an hour. That helps the application team connect scattered failures and decide whether a carefully protected crash recording is needed.
hardware: Windows systems that log Application Error Event 1000. Application ownership/version inventory is required for routing.
